blanks.note: Banco Central de la Republica Argentina, Estados Contables al 31 de diciembre de 2025 (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/archivos/Pdfs/PublicacionesEstadisticas/informes/estados-contables-2025.pdf) and the 2024 set (e2024estadosContables.pdf), both downloaded and the whole text grepped, accounting-policy notes (nota 3) as well as the reserves notes. Searched for externamente, administrador, gestor, 'gestion delegada', RAMP, Banco Mundial, BIRF, Crown Agents, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street, Nomura, custodi, mandato. Nota 4.1 'Reservas Internacionales' breaks the reserves into oro (1,984.96 oz troy), divisas (current accounts at foreign correspondent banks and overnight) and 4.1.3 'Colocaciones realizables en divisas' (time deposits, sight deposits, foreign public securities, repos) and names no manager and no firm. Nota 7.2 says the Investment Policies are set by the Directorio 'a propuesta de la Gerencia Principal de Administracion de Reservas' and that the risks are monitored daily by the BCRA's own risk area - management is internal. The counterparty disclosure is a percentage table by group (Supranacionales y Bancos Centrales, Soberanos, Billetes, Otras Contrapartes Financieras, Otros Organismos Multilaterales) with no firm named at all. BIRF appears only as IDB/IBRD provincial on-lending and as capital subscriptions ('Aportes al BID, BIRF, AIF'); BIS appears only as a dividend received and a 12-month credit facility agreement. No outside reserve manager.

Brunei Darussalam Central Bank 2025 Annual Report (cms.bdcb.gov.bn/storage/uploads/publications/17824568929284490.pdf, 21 MB, includes the full consolidated financial statements) and the 2023 Annual Report (17156676945135910.pdf), both downloaded and grepped end to end including the accounting-policy notes. BDCB confirms the MECHANISM twice but names no firm. Governance section: the Investment Advisory Committee 'oversees the selection and appointment of external fund managers and supports performance evaluations to ensure effective investment management' (2025, as at 31 December 2025; same wording in 2023). Note 27.2.1 Credit risk: 'The Group Risk Committee manages and controls credit risk by monitoring the investment guidelines and directives issued to the fund managers of the Group.' The 2023 report's ESG section adds 'the Central Bank has appointed a fund manager to manage an ESG mandate since 2022'. No firm is named anywhere in either report - no RAMP, World Bank, Crown Agents, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, State Street or Nomura hit except 'Deposit from World Bank', which is a liability line. Credit exposure is described as securities of Singapore, Hong Kong and China sovereigns. So Brunei demonstrably uses external fund managers, including an ESG mandate running since 2022, and publishes none of their names. Also downloaded and grepped the 2024 and 2025 Financial Stability Reports and the 2024 FIU Annual Report: nothing. Next document: BDCB procurement or tender notices for fund-management services, or an IMF Article IV safeguards discussion.

Second document now read, so this is no longer only an old-report test. IMF Country Report, Bhutan 2024 Article IV consultation (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2024/english/1btnea2024001-print-pdf.pdf, 235,000 characters) downloaded and grepped for external manager, externally managed, fund manager, RAMP, Reserve Advisory, Crown Agents, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, custodian and reserve management. The only reserve-management passages are paragraph 44 and the Board assessment: 'RMA's efforts to strengthen its reserve management strategy in collaboration with SARTTAC are welcome'. SARTTAC is the IMF's South Asia regional training and technical assistance centre, so that is technical assistance and not a management mandate, and the brief excludes it. 'One fund manager' appears only in a count of licensed domestic financial institutions. No outside manager of the RMA's reserves anywhere. Combined with round 68's end-to-end grep of the RMA Annual Reports 2003/04 and 2007/08, two independent document types now name none. Still outstanding: the RMA's own recent annual reports on rma.org.bt, which no search this round or last returned.

SAFE Annual Report 2023 (https://www.safe.gov.cn/en/file/file/20231229/72bf9574b78c4f1da844ad75d46b0226.pdf, 320,000 characters) and SAFE Annual Report 2022 (20221226/9186b372d33e4a6b9d156ab154cc2979.pdf, 290,000 characters), both downloaded and grepped end to end. The MECHANISM is confirmed and no firm is named. The Reserves Management Department's published functions include that it 'supervises and inspects the status of external-managed reserve assets' (same sentence in both years), and the same list ends with 'studies and draws up principles for the operation of other entrusted foreign exchange assets'. So SAFE states on its own face that part of the reserves is externally managed, and names no manager. The SAFE Investment Center is described as responsible for 'the operation and management of official foreign exchange reserves and gold reserves' - that is SAFE's own affiliated institution, a central-bank-subsidiary question and not an outside manager for this row. UBS (China) Limited, UBS SDIC Fund Management, BlackRock CCB Wealth Management and State Street Corp Beijing Branch appear only in the appendix lists of licensed foreign banks, QDII and wealth-management institutions in China - licence lists, not mandates. No RAMP, World Bank, Crown Agents, Amundi, PIMCO, Wellington or Nomura mandate. Next document: the PBoC Annual Report, or the SAFE 2019 report (20190905/8bed0ab4a8f74ef08b0b3553c5d66ac3.pdf, which returned zero bytes to curl this round and was not retried).

No Central Bank of Egypt document opened, for the second round running, and the reason now looks structural rather than a search failure. Three searches this round and last, including one restricted to cbe.org.eg and one on 'Notes to the financial statements', returned no CBE annual report and no CBE audited financial statements anywhere - every statements PDF returned belongs to an Egyptian commercial bank (Credit Agricole Egypt on ca-egypt.com, Export Development Bank on eg-bank.com, EG Bank, First Bank) and every CBE item is either a monthly External Position bulletin, a monthly Reserve Money M0 release, or press coverage of the CBE's monthly balance sheet.
